positions.catalyst: FEED VERIFIED LIVE BEFORE ANY PRICING, AND THE FIRST PULL PROVED WHY THAT CHECK IS NOT CEREMONIAL. My first proxy call at 2026-09-09T00:11:08Z returned asOf=2026-08-27T10:45:05Z with BTC-USD 79,602.37 — a TWELVE-DAY-OLD CACHED RESPONSE. Had I priced off it I would have booked a fabricated +$96 gain instead of the real loss. I retried per the rules and the second call returned asOf=2026-09-09T00:11:24.899Z, BTC-USD 78,626.99 / SPY 765.96 / SOXL 123.27, and every subsequent batch carried a live asOf. Cross-check against Robinhood at 20:11:30 ET: BTC mark 78,676.62 (0.06% from proxy), ETH proxy 2,493.60 vs RH 2,493.71 (exact), SOL proxy 103.67 vs RH 103.73. Independent equity confirmation: Robinhood's own daily bar for SOXL on 9/8 (real, volume 51.86M, not interpolated) closed 123.27, identical to the proxy, and get_equity_quotes returns sip-list-exchange-close 123.27 for 9/8. THE FEED IS LIVE ON BOTH ASSET CLASSES. New finding for the record: the staleness is not a premarket-vs-RTH property as the last three runs concluded — it is a CACHE that can serve an arbitrarily old response on a cold call. THE FIX IS TO ALWAYS PULL TWICE AND REJECT ANY asOf NOT WITHIN MINUTES OF NOW. PROCESS GAP, STATED PLAINLY: no run fired on 9/1, 9/2, 9/3, 9/4, or 9/8 morning. The BTC position was carried from 8/31 through six full sessions instead of rotating daily. That is the second consecutive multi-session carry caused by the scheduler, not by a decision. CLOSED BTC-USD AT 78,626.99 FOR -$43.07 (-0.38%). The post-mortem matters more than the number, because the thesis was not merely wrong — it was wrong in the specific way I warned it might be. I wrote on 8/31 that my strongest arguments were 'about plumbing, not about markets' and that stripping them out left 'a one-day relative-strength observation plus a range-bound chart, which is a thin edge.' That is exactly what happened: BTC went sideways for six sessions and COIN gave back the entire bounce I read as demand (188.12 close on 8/31 -> 184.64 on 9/4 -> 178.94 now, -4.9%). The relative-strength signal was mean reversion, as the risks section said it might be. WORSE, I EXPLICITLY IDENTIFIED THE WINNING TRADE AND PASSED ON IT. I rejected ERX and OILU on 8/31 arguing the war premium would bleed out, citing the USO 8/21-to-8/25 -6.3% leg as proof of how fast that happens, and I named the branch where I would 'lose on both the position and the omission.' That branch is the one that happened: USO 133.70 -> 146.03 (+9.2%), UCO 44.61 -> 49.35 (+10.6%), ERX 108.34 -> 111.27, XLE 63.96 -> 64.77, while my defensive spot pick did nothing. The reasoning error is namable: I treated 'defense stocks are not rallying' as evidence the market disbelieved the conflict. Defense equities price multi-year procurement cycles; crude prices barrels this month. They were answering different questions and I let the wrong one veto the trade. TODAY'S TAPE. Regular session (official 9/8 closes vs 9/4): USO 146.03 (+2.87%), UCO 49.35 (+4.33%), BNO 57.73 (+2.89%), GUSH 47.38 (+3.22%), ERX 111.27 (+2.37%), XOP 193.91 (+1.68%), XLE 64.77 (+1.11%), OIH 428.57 (+0.24%); inverses confirm — SCO 21.57 (-3.88%), DRIP 32.80 (-3.33%), ERY 8.71. Broad tape lower: the Dow fell more than 600 points to 52,786.07, the S&P 500 closed 7,673.52 and the Nasdaq 26,421.41, with SPY 765.96, QQQ 718.36, TQQQ 72.16 (-0.29%), NVDA 225.73 (-2.01%), MU 1,000.26 (-1.61%). Per the Motley Fool and Yahoo Finance wraps, an unexpectedly strong jobs report pushed September rate-HIKE expectations up and Treasury yields with them; TLT 82.20, TMV 42.44. Semis were the one pocket of strength (SOXL 123.27 +5.11%, SMH 573.73). Crypto is the weak tape now, not the strong one: COIN 178.94, MSTR 136.52, BITX 17.59, IBIT 44.39, BTC 78,627, ETH 2,493.60, SOL 103.67. Gold FELL on a war day again — GLD 399.72 (-1.73%), NUGT 188.48 — because real yields are rising. Volatility refuses to bid: VIX 15.72, UVXY 17.93. THE DECISIVE FACT IS WHAT HAPPENED AFTER THE 4PM BELL, AND IT IS NOT IN ANY EQUITY PRICE YET. WTI SETTLED at 93.03 today (+1.69%). Right now, at 00:13:04Z, CL=F is 94.52 and BZ=F is 99.41. Crude is trading 1.60% ABOVE its own settlement while every US oil ETF sits frozen at a mark that reflects 93.03. The reason is on the tape: per CNBC, NBC News and CBS, Iran-aligned Houthi forces hit Saudi Aramco installations and energy infrastructure at Abha, Khamis Mushait, Jazan and Najran, wounding at least 73; Saudi Arabia's Energy Ministry said operations at SEVERAL OIL FACILITIES AND UTILITIES HAVE BEEN SUSPENDED with firefighters still containing blazes. US forces then struck IRGC-linked oil tankers. LATE TUESDAY — after the US close — Iranian state media (Mehr) reported successive explosions on KHARG ISLAND, which handles up to 90% of Iran's crude exports, and at Jask. Oil spiked a second time inside 24 hours on that report. Brent touched 99 and is knocking on 100.
positions.driver: LONG UCO — PROSHARES ULTRA BLOOMBERG CRUDE OIL, 2X DAILY WTI FUTURES — 100% of capital (226.031932 shares) at 49.48, stop 45.52 (-8%, the 2x band). (1) THE EDGE IS A DATED, MEASURABLE GAP BETWEEN TWO MARKETS THAT ARE NOT BOTH OPEN. UCO's mark of record is the 4pm settle of 49.35, and that settle prices WTI at 93.03. WTI is 94.52 right now. At 2x daily exposure that is roughly a 3.2% move already banked in the underlying that the ETF has not been able to express, because its shares stopped trading and crude futures did not. This is not a forecast; it is an accounting identity between a closed wrapper and an open underlying. Everything else in this thesis is about whether that gap survives the night. (2) THE CATALYST IS PHYSICAL BARRELS, NOT SENTIMENT, AND THAT IS THE DISTINCTION I GOT WRONG LAST WEEK. On 8/31 the bull case was a risk PREMIUM — a fear bid on headlines, which decays. Tonight Saudi Arabia's own Energy Ministry has CONFIRMED SUSPENDED OPERATIONS at multiple facilities, US forces have destroyed IRGC-linked tankers, and Kharg Island — the terminal for up to 90% of Iranian exports — is reporting explosions. Supply that is physically offline does not mean-revert on a de-escalation tweet; it reverts when the equipment restarts. The whole reason my 8/31 fade was wrong is that I priced a premium when the market was pricing a shortage. (3) THE SUPPLY BUFFER IS THIN, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES THE PAYOFF ASYMMETRIC RATHER THAN MERELY DIRECTIONAL. OPEC spare capacity is roughly 2.5 mb/d after the UAE's exit, OPEC+ held October production STEADY rather than adding barrels, US crude inventories are falling, diesel is tight, and Hormuz tanker traffic is at its lowest since May. Kharg alone is on the order of 1.5 mb/d. With a buffer that small, incremental disruption maps convexly into price — Goldman's stated upside case is 120 on intensifying shipping attacks against a downside of 80 on normalization. That skew, taken at 2x with a hard stop, is the asymmetry the mandate asks for. (4) 2X IS THE DELIBERATE CHOICE OVER 3X AND OVER 1X, AND I CAN DEFEND BOTH DIRECTIONS. Against 3x: the catalyst is fresh and real but headline-reversible, and OILU's 3x wrapper printed +2.16% today against XOP's +1.68% — tracking that loose on a 136k-share ETN is a wrapper I do not want carrying 100% of the book overnight. Against 1x USO: at +2.87% on a day WTI settled +1.69%, USO gives up too much of a 15-hour edge to be worth the same overnight gap risk. UCO traded 3.03M shares today, has a real verified 9/8 bar, and tracks the futures curve directly rather than through equity beta. (5) THE ENTRY IS INSIDE THE CHASE BAN AND I AM PAYING THE HONEST PRICE, NOT THE FLATTERING ONE. UCO is +4.33% on the session, comfortably under the 8-10% ban. The canonical proxy prints 49.35, but Robinhood's after-hours book is already 49.46 bid / 49.55 ask with a last trade of 49.48 at 00:13:49Z. Booking 49.35 would be claiming a fill I could not get, so I am entering at 49.48 — the worse number — and marking the exit leg the same conservative way (BTC out at the proxy's 78,626.99, below Robinhood's 78,676.62 mark). Both legs err against the book. (6) CRUDE'S OWN CHART IS A CONFIRMED BREAKOUT, NOT A ONE-DAY SPIKE. UCO ran 44.61 (8/31) -> 47.43 -> 47.29 -> 46.72 -> 47.30 -> 49.35, and today's 48.75 open / 49.35 close / 48.35 low held entirely above the prior week's range. The consolidation on 9/2-9/4 digested the first escalation leg without giving it back, and today broke out on the second. Compare the failed pattern I cited last week — USO's 8/21-to-8/25 collapse — which had no confirmed production outage behind it. This one does. (7) WHY NOT SOMETHING ELSE ENTIRELY. The rest of the board is either weak or catalyst-free tonight, which raises the relative value of the one instrument with a live, dated, unpriced event. CHOSEN OVER: (1) SCO / DRIP, FADING THE SPIKE at 21.57 / 32.80 — this is the trade I actually made the equivalent of last week and it cost me the week's biggest move. Rejected again, and now for a better reason than the last one: with Kharg burning and Saudi facilities offline, a 2x SHORT crude position held unstopped through an overnight session where futures trade and my ETF does not is the definition of the wrong tail. (2) OILU 3X at 55.81 — the highest-beta expression of the correct view. Rejected on wrapper quality: +2.16% today versus XOP +1.68% is tracking that does not resemble 3x, on 136k shares. (3) GUSH 2X E&P at 47.38 and ERX 2X ENERGY at 111.27 — same direction through equity beta. Rejected because equities discount a normalized strip while futures price the barrel that is missing tonight; XLE managed only +1.11% against UCO's +4.33%, which is the market telling me where the transmission is. (4) USO 1X at 146.03 and BNO 1X BRENT at 57.73 — BNO is arguably the purer instrument since Brent at 99.41 is the benchmark actually reflecting Hormuz risk. Rejected on payoff: 1x wearing full overnight gap risk. (5) OIH at 428.57 — services barely moved (+0.24%) and has stalled under its 9/2 close of 436.58 for four sessions. No participation, no thesis. (6) SPOT BTC / ETH / SOL, i.e. REPEATING LAST WEEK'S PICK — the honest defensive option, and the one with a continuously-tradable stop. Rejected because the signal has flipped against it: COIN 178.94 has now given back the entire bounce I built the 8/31 thesis on, BTC has gone nowhere for six sessions, and rising real yields on a hike-odds repricing are a direct headwind. Choosing it again would be choosing measurability over edge twice. (7) SOXL at 123.27 (+5.11%) — the day's strongest leveraged move, and precisely why I will not buy it at the close of that move with no scheduled catalyst before my exit. (8) MU at 1,000.26 — best trend on the board, but it FELL 1.61% today and earnings are still weeks out. (9) LONG VOLATILITY via UVXY at 17.93 — VIX 15.72 with a shooting war and oil at 99 is genuinely cheap insurance, and this was the closest call after UCO. Rejected because vol has now refused to bid through three separate escalation days; buying a decaying instrument that will not respond to its own catalyst is paying for a signal that is not firing. (10) NUGT / GLD — gold fell 1.73% on a war day for the second week running. That is information about gold, not a setup. (11) TMV 3X INVERSE TREASURIES at 42.44 — rate direction is right, but it went nowhere today (+0.09%) despite the hike-odds repricing, and it is the same wrong-part-of-the-curve trade I rejected last week. (12) 100% CASH — rejected. There is a dated, unpriced, physically-caused event tonight and a liquid 2x wrapper to express it in; that is the setup this book exists to take.
positions.risks: THE SINGLE LARGEST RISK IS THAT I AM NOW OVERCORRECTING FOR LAST WEEK'S MISS, AND I WANT THAT ON THE RECORD BEFORE THE OUTCOME IS KNOWN. Seven days ago I wrote a long, careful argument for why the war premium would bleed out. It did not, and I lost the week's best move. Today I am buying the same trade at a price 10.6% higher, and the loudest voice in my reasoning is 'I was wrong to pass.' That is regret, and regret is not an edge. The strongest version of the bear case is uncomfortable and simple: the informed money bought this at 44.61 and I am buying it at 49.48. THE OVERNIGHT GAP IS UNSTOPPED AND THIS IS A 2X WRAPPER. UCO does not trade while crude does. If a ceasefire, a credible de-escalation signal, an SPR release, or a Saudi statement that facilities are restarting lands at 3am, WTI gaps down and UCO opens through my 45.52 stop with no opportunity to exit at it. The stop is a level in a file, not a resting order. This is precisely the objection I used to reject energy on 8/31, and it has not become less true — I am now accepting it rather than refusing it, because the catalyst is a confirmed outage rather than a fear bid. That is a real distinction, but it is a judgment, not a proof. MY CENTRAL EDGE HAS A SHORT SHELF LIFE AND MAY ALREADY BE LEAKING. The 1.60% futures-over-settle gap is real at 00:13Z, but Robinhood's after-hours book has already moved UCO to 49.48 and USO to 146.56 — roughly 0.3% of it is priced. If the remaining gap closes overnight in thin trading rather than at tomorrow's open, I will have paid up for an edge that was arbitraged away while I held. Conversely, if crude simply retraces to its 93.03 settle by morning, the gap vanishes and I am long a 2x product with no compensation. CONTANGO AND DAILY REBALANCING ERODE THIS INSTRUMENT ON ANY HOLD LONGER THAN INTENDED, AND MY HOLDS HAVE NOT BEEN THE INTENDED LENGTH. UCO resets 2x daily and rolls futures; in a choppy or contangoed tape it decays against a buy-and-hold in the underlying. My last two positions were carried for four and six sessions because scheduled runs did not fire. If that happens again here, path dependency works against me in a way it did not against unlevered spot BTC. This is the most likely mechanism by which a correct directional call still loses money. THE MACRO REGIME IS ACTIVELY HOSTILE TO EVERYTHING ELSE, WHICH CUTS BOTH WAYS. A strong jobs print raised September hike odds, the Dow fell 600 points, and higher crude feeds straight into the inflation print. If oil above 95 is read as a demand-destroying tax rather than a supply squeeze, energy equities and eventually the crude curve itself sell off with the tape. Backwardated spikes on geopolitics have historically been the fastest to unwind of any commodity move. THE COUNTER-EVIDENCE I AM CHOOSING TO DISCOUNT, STATED FAIRLY. XLE managed only +1.11% and OIH +0.24% today. I have framed that as equities discounting a normalized strip while futures price tonight's missing barrel — but the honest alternative reading is that the equity market, which owns the assets that produce the oil, does not believe this price is durable. That is the mirror image of the defense-stock argument I used incorrectly last week, and I am now on the other side of the same kind of inference. I do not get to use 'equities know something' when it suits me and 'equities answer a different question' when it does not. Both readings are available; I have picked one. AN EXPLICIT ADMISSION ON MY OWN PRICING RULE. Canonical procedure says the proxy price is the price of record, which would be 49.35. I am entering at 49.48 because that is what Robinhood's live after-hours book says a fill costs, and taking the lower number would manufacture 0.26% of fictional performance. I believe deviating toward the conservative number is right, but it IS a deviation and the next run should know it was deliberate. THE CACHE BUG IS THE MOST IMPORTANT UNRESOLVED DEFECT IN THIS BOOK. My first price call tonight returned a twelve-day-old snapshot with a live-looking payload and no error. Three prior runs diagnosed this as a premarket-vs-RTH lag; that diagnosis was wrong. It is a cache that can serve stale data at ANY hour. FOR THE NEXT RUN: pull the proxy TWICE, compare asOf to wall-clock, reject anything older than a few minutes, and cross-check at least one equity against Robinhood's sip-list-exchange-close and one crypto against the Robinhood mark before pricing a single fill. Tonight that check caught a $96 phantom gain. THE SCHEDULER REMAINS BROKEN AND IT IS NOW MATERIAL. Runs did not fire on 9/1 through 9/7. A book whose entire risk model assumes daily rotation has rotated twice in nine days. Until that is fixed, every position here is effectively a multi-day hold in a daily-reset leveraged product, and the stated stops are dormant for the duration. EXECUTION NOTES. Entry 49.48 = Robinhood after-hours last trade at 2026-09-09T00:13:49.816Z, against proxy/official close 49.35 (sip-list-exchange-close, 9/8) and an AH book of 49.46 x 49.55. Exit of BTC at 78,626.99 = proxy asOf 2026-09-09T00:11:24.899Z, cross-checked to Robinhood mark 78,676.62 at 20:11:30 ET, 0.06% apart; I took the lower. UCO traded 3,028,783 shares on 9/8 — liquid, fractionable, no tradability flag. MITIGANTS: 2x rather than 3x; entry +4.33% on the day, well inside the chase ban; the underlying is a confirmed physical outage rather than a sentiment bid; OPEC spare capacity near 2.5 mb/d gives the convexity a real structural basis; both legs priced conservatively against the book; and the position is in the single most liquid crude wrapper available, so the exit mark will be real whenever the next run fires.
